newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ says its MCI has done an "admirable" job.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ says its MCI has done an "admirable" job.

text.p: The Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Friday the central bank believed its Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) has done its job admirably.

In a letter to the National Business Review (NBR) magazine replying to a Reuters column published a week ago, Murray Sherwin took issue with accusations levelled by BNZ economist Peter Jolly that the MCI has spurred interest rate volatility, uncertainty and confusion.
"Has the MCI created confusion? The evidence certainly does not point that way," Sherwin wrote.
Jolly's concerns were "misplaced", Sherwin added, because it was a clear misreading of the causal links to blame the MCI for recent interest rate volatility.
"We have been experiencing a period of high volatility in exchange rates, both here and abroad.
"It is hardly surprising that domestic interest rates have reflected some of that turbulence and associated uncertainty," he added.
The RBNZ brought in the current version of the MCI with its June Monetary Policy Statement, creating a datum line of 825 basis points indicating its current prefered mix of conditions.
Initially it said it would hope to see conditions remaining within a 50 basis point band of this level.
In June, RB Governor Don Brash said that as the bank's quarterly statement receded into history the bank would be more tolerant of moves outside its identified band.
"I suggest he (Jolly) rereads the comments Don Brash made in June when discussing the degree of MCI variation that the bank was likely to accept without reaction," Sherwin said.
"He will then find that the bank been entirely consistent with those comments."
Sherwin said evidence indicated the MCI was not creating confusion.
"The fact is that a substantial adjustment in the exchange rate has occurred without the Reserve Bank being drawn into public comment, much less market actions.
"Far from being confused, it seems that financial market had an uncommonly clear understanding of the Reserve Bank's stance."
The MCI was at 716, 109 points below the 825 level late on Friday morning. The bank in June forecast the index would average 785 in the December quarter.
